samples.summary: New doc bullet asserts a global invariant ("Identifiers are URL-encoded into the previewed path exactly as the client encodes them") that the import/upload previews do not satisfy
samples.evidence: cli.md:836-841 states the encoding invariant unconditionally, and 824-830 claims "A dry run never reaches the network" across the CLI. But the import previews were left untouched by this change: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:155 prints `path: `/documents/${replace}/content`` with a RAW, unencoded id (same in slides/import.ts:177+, notes/import.ts:142+, files/upload.ts:171). Those previews also emit a different envelope — `{ method, path, body }` with no `dry_run: true` and no absolute `url` — so they neither go through `printDryRun` nor honour the documented shape shown at cli.md:813-820. The change hardened and documented one half of the dry-run surface while the doc speaks for all of it.

samples.summary: Preview URLs are hand-mirrored from HttpClient in several places instead of being derived from one URL builder, so "the preview is the request" is enforced only by comment
samples.evidence: `apiKeysUrl()` (api-keys.ts:14-19) re-derives `${server}/workspaces/${workspace}/api-keys[/id]`, which HttpClient already builds three times (http-client.ts:397, in createApiKey, and :415 revokeApiKey). Likewise cells.ts:24-29 re-implements HttpClient.getCells/getCell's endpoint choice and range encoding, and sheets-export.ts:47-53 re-implements the `?range=` query. Every one of these carries a comment saying it "mirrors" the client — the repo's stated preference is reuse (shared builders), and the fit-correct shape here is exporting a path/URL builder from HttpClient that both the client and the preview consume, so the two cannot drift.

samples.summary: `seg()` is defined twice with identical bodies (dry-run.ts exported, http-client.ts private)

One home (or a re-export) would keep the "same encoding as the client" claim structural rather than by convention.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out exactly. docs/design/cli.md:836-841 states the URL-encoding invariant unconditionally ("Identifiers are URL-encoded into the previewed path exactly as the client encodes them into the real request"), and cli.md:813-820 documents the preview envelope as {dry_run, method, url, body}; cli.md:846-849 explicitly places `docs import` / `notes import` / `slides import` under this same dry-run section. But those previews bypass the hardened helper entirely: packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:155 emits `path: `/documents/${replace}/content`` with a raw, unencoded id, as do notes/import.ts:147 and slides/import.ts:182; files/upload.ts:171-181 likewise emits `{method, path, body}` with no `dry_run` flag and no absolute `url`. `seg()` (client/dry-run.ts:12-14) and `printDryRun` (client/dry-run.ts:22-52) are referenced only from commands/* and client/*, never from the four import/upload modules, so no caller-side guard normalises them. The doc therefore asserts a global invariant and envelope shape that half the documented dry-run surface does not satisfy — a real design-doc/implementation conformance mismatch in the design-fit lane, not a taste preference. No refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists as described (api-keys.ts:13-18 mirrors http-client.ts:396-397/403-404/414-415; cells.ts:24-29 mirrors http-client.ts:356-368; sheets-export.ts:47-53 mirrors the ?range= query), but it is not a blocking fit violation. The originating task explicitly prescribes this shape ("mirror the three client paths the handler picks between… Encode the range the same way HttpClient.getCells does", todo:21-24; "printDryRun grew a printDryRunUrl sibling" for the non-v1 api-keys base, todo:40-43), and its Non-goals/acceptance criteria (todo:50-60) are met — the printed envelope matches the request and no network call happens. docs/design/cli.md §8.2 (809-844) specifies dry-run behavior (URL equality and identical segment encoding), not a shared URL-builder abstraction, and cli.md:713 defines dry-run.ts as a request printer taking a path. The hand-written path pattern is the repo-wide convention (52 printDryRun/printDryRunUrl call sites across 10 command files), so this is not reinvention of an existing module; extracting path builders from HttpClient is a "could be cleaner" refactor preference, i.e. minor/nit under this lens's rubric, which never blocks.

searchedFor: read notes.ts, files.ts, slides.ts, api-keys.ts, sheets-export.ts action bodies
finding.summary: New design-doc bullet overstates the behaviour: "A dry run never reaches the network" is now a universal claim, but many read commands still fetch under --dry-run
finding.evidence: The added bullet reads: "Reads honour the flag too: `docs list`, `docs get`, `sheets tabs list`, and `sheets cells get` print their GET without fetching. A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless." The second sentence is a blanket guarantee, yet in the same tree `notes list` (packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35), `notes get` (:76), `slides list`/`slides get` (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:35,76), `files list`/`files get` (packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:85,105), `sheets export` (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:39) and `api-keys list` (packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:31) all issue the request regardless of `opts.dryRun`. A design doc that promises an invariant the implementation only partially satisfies is worse than an enumerated list; either scope the sentence to the four commands or cover the rest.

verdict.reason: Both halves of the presence claim fail. (a) The quoted doc text does not exist: docs/design/cli.md:824-830 reads "Reads honour the flag too, in every namespace: `docs list`/`get`/`content`/`export`, `notes list`/`get`/`content`/`export`, `slides list`/`get`/`content`/`export`, `files list`/`get`/`download`, `sheets tabs list`, `sheets cells get`, `sheets export`, and `api-keys list` print their GET without fetching" — it is not scoped to four commands and already enumerates the very namespaces the reviewer says are omitted. (b) Every command named as fetching regardless of --dry-run in fact short-circuits with printDryRun + early return before any getClient() call: notes list (notes.ts:35-40), notes get (:82-85), notes content (:145-148), notes export (:205-208), slides list (slides.ts:40-45), slides get (:87-90), slides content (:151-154), slides export (:207-210), files list (files.ts:87-92), files get (:113-116), files download (:58-61), sheets export (sheets-export.ts:44-56, network call at :58 is after the guarded return), api-keys list (api-keys.ts:52-55). The cited line numbers correspond to .command()/.action() registration or input validation, not unguarded fetches. The doc's invariant therefore matches the implementation and there is no spec-conformance gap under the design-fit lens.
